proof_summary: Writing \(d=D(n)=ge\), where \(g\) contains the factors 2 and 5 and \(\gcd(e,10)=1\), the proof solves \(n+9B\equiv0\pmod e\) and uses repeated decimal blocks of length \(L\) with \(10^L\equiv1\pmod e\) to construct \(C\) with \(D(C)=n\) and \(e\mid C\). Then \(k=10^dC\) has \(D(k)=n\) and \(d\mid k\) because \(g\mid10^d\); moreover \(k\ne n\), since a positive multiple of 10 has digit sum strictly smaller than itself.
